passages.title: 籃球場上的膝蓋傷
passages.text: Kevin is the tallest player on our school basketball team. Last Friday, during an important game, he jumped high to catch the ball. When he came down, he landed badly and fell. He held his right {1} and could not stand up. The coach ran over and put ice on it. "Don't move," he said. Kevin's face was red, and he looked like he wanted to {2}. The next day, the doctor told him to rest for two weeks. Kevin was sad because he could not play. But he did not give up. He sat on the bench at every game and shouted for his team. He also did exercises to make the muscles around his {3} stronger. Two weeks later, he came back to the court. In his first game back, he scored twenty points. After the game, his teammates carried him on their {4}. "Your knee is fine now," the coach laughed, "but please be {5} when you land!"

blanks.why: 跌倒後抱著右「膝蓋」knee 站不起來。museum（博物館）、village（村莊）、meal（一餐）都不是身體部位，不能用 his right 修飾、也不能抱著喊痛。
痛得好像快「哭」了 wanted to cry。bake（烘烤）、paint（畫）、marry（結婚）放在這裡完全不合理。
做運動讓「膝蓋」周圍的肌肉更強壯：the muscles around his knees。museums、villages、meals 周圍沒有「他的肌肉」。
carry someone on one's shoulders「把某人扛在肩膀上」，慶祝勝利的常見動作。tickets（票）、meals、letters（信）上面不能扛人。
be careful「小心」：落地時要小心。crowded（擁擠的）、delicious（好吃的）、thirsty（口渴的）都不能用來提醒人落地的動作。

passages.zh: Kevin 是我們學校籃球隊最高的球員。上週五一場重要的比賽中，他跳得很高去接球，落下時姿勢不好，跌倒了。他抱著右膝蓋站不起來。教練跑過來幫他冰敷。「不要動。」他說。Kevin 的臉漲得通紅，看起來快要哭了。隔天，醫生要他休息兩個星期。Kevin 很難過，因為他不能打球，但他沒有放棄。每場比賽他都坐在板凳上為隊友加油，也做運動讓膝蓋周圍的肌肉更強壯。兩週後，他回到球場。復出的第一場比賽，他就得了二十分。比賽結束後，隊友們把他扛在肩膀上。「你的膝蓋現在沒事了，」教練笑著說，「但落地的時候請小心一點！」

passages.title: 會轉頭的貓頭鷹
passages.text: At the zoo, our class stopped in front of a big owl. It sat on a branch and looked at us with its round yellow eyes. "Watch this," said the zookeeper. She walked slowly behind the tree. The owl did not move its body at all. It only turned its {1} and kept looking at her! "Wow, its head went all the way around!" shouted Tim. "Not all the way," the zookeeper explained. "An owl can turn its head about 270 degrees. Its eyes cannot move like ours, so it needs a very {2} neck." Then she told us another fact. "An owl often eats a mouse in one bite. The mouse goes down its {3} and into its {4}. Later, the owl brings up the bones and fur in a small ball." Everyone said, "Ew!" but we all wanted to learn more. On the bus home, Tim tried to turn his head like an owl. "Ouch! My {5} hurts!" he cried.

blanks.why: 身體不動，只轉動「脖子」turned its neck。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、meal（一餐）都不是貓頭鷹身上能轉動的部位。
眼睛不能轉，所以需要一個很「特別的」脖子 a very special neck。crowded（擁擠的）、thirsty（口渴的）、lonely（孤單的）不能形容脖子。
老鼠被吞下去會經過「喉嚨」goes down its throat。pocket（口袋）、corner（角落）、bill（帳單）都不是食物經過的地方。
食物最後進到「胃」into its stomach。museum（博物館）、ticket、village 都不在身體裡。
學貓頭鷹轉頭，結果「脖子」痛 My neck hurts。meal、letter（信）、bill 都不會「痛」。

passages.zh: 在動物園裡，我們班停在一隻大貓頭鷹前面。牠站在樹枝上，用圓圓的黃眼睛看著我們。「看好喔。」管理員說。她慢慢走到樹後面，貓頭鷹的身體完全沒動，只轉動脖子，一直盯著她看！「哇，牠的頭轉了一整圈！」Tim 大喊。「不是一整圈，」管理員解釋，「貓頭鷹的頭大約可以轉 270 度。牠的眼睛不能像我們一樣轉動，所以需要一個非常特別的脖子。」接著她又告訴我們另一件事：「貓頭鷹常常一口就吞下一隻老鼠，老鼠經過喉嚨進到胃裡。之後，貓頭鷹會把骨頭和毛吐成一顆小球。」大家都喊「噁！」，但我們都想知道更多。坐公車回家時，Tim 試著像貓頭鷹一樣轉頭。「哎喲！我的脖子好痛！」他叫道。

passages.title: 失去聲音的班長
passages.text: Amy was our class leader, and she was also the best singer in our class. The school singing contest was on Friday, and she had a solo part. On Wednesday, she woke up with a sore {1} and could hardly speak. "Drink warm water with honey," said her mom. "And don't talk too much." At school, Amy wrote everything on paper {2} of talking. Her friends thought it was fun, so they wrote notes back to her. On Thursday, her throat felt better, but her voice was still {3}. On Friday morning, she put a scarf around her {4} to keep it warm. When it was time for her solo, she took a deep breath, put her hand on her {5}, and sang. Her voice was not perfect, but it was clear and beautiful. Our class won second place. After the contest, Amy laughed and finally said, "Thank you, everyone!" in her real voice.

blanks.why: a sore throat「喉嚨痛」，所以幾乎說不出話。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、letter（信）不會「痛」，也和說不出話無關。
instead of + V-ing「用…代替…」：用寫的代替說話。ahead（在前面）、either（兩者之一）、abroad（在國外）都不能接 of talking 表示「代替」。
聲音還是很「虛弱」her voice was still weak。cheap（便宜的）、fresh（新鮮的）、wet（溼的）不能形容生病後的聲音。
把圍巾圍在「脖子」上保暖 put a scarf around her neck。bill（帳單）、meal（一餐）、ticket 都不能圍圍巾。
唱歌前深呼吸，把手放在「肚子」上 put her hand on her stomach。ticket、village、museum（博物館）都不在她身上。

passages.zh: Amy 是我們的班長，也是班上最會唱歌的人。學校的歌唱比賽在星期五，她負責一段獨唱。星期三，她一醒來就喉嚨痛，幾乎說不出話。「喝加蜂蜜的溫水，」媽媽說，「而且不要講太多話。」在學校，Amy 用紙寫字代替說話。朋友們覺得很好玩，也寫紙條回她。星期四，她的喉嚨好一點了，但聲音還是很虛弱。星期五早上，她把圍巾圍在脖子上保暖。輪到她獨唱時，她深吸一口氣，把手放在肚子上，開口唱歌。她的聲音不完美，卻清楚又好聽。我們班得了第二名。比賽結束後，Amy 笑了，終於用真正的聲音說：「謝謝大家！」

passages.title: 夜市吃太飽
passages.text: On Saturday night, my cousin Leo and I went to Shilin Night Market. Leo said, "I am so {1} that I can eat everything here!" First, we ate a big piece of fried chicken. Then we had stinky tofu, oyster omelets, and bubble tea. Leo kept eating. "Are you sure you are okay?" I asked. "No problem," he said, patting his {2}. One hour later, Leo sat on a chair with a sad face. "My {3} hurts," he said. "I ate too much." I bought him a bottle of warm water. He drank it slowly, but then he said, "Something is coming up my {4}!" We ran to the restroom just in time. On the way home, Leo was very quiet. He did not even want to look at the food stands. "Next time," he said, "I will stop when I feel {5}."

blanks.why: so hungry that I can eat everything「餓到什麼都吃得下」。lonely（孤單的）、honest（誠實的）、polite（有禮貌的）和「什麼都吃得下」沒有因果關係。
pat one's stomach「拍拍肚子」，表示自己還吃得下。ticket（票）、museum（博物館）、village（村莊）都不是身體部位。
吃太多所以「肚子痛」My stomach hurts。corner（角落）、letter（信）、pocket（口袋）不會痛。
東西從「喉嚨」湧上來，快吐了 coming up my throat。bill（帳單）、ticket、village 都不是食物經過的地方。
feel full「覺得飽了」：下次覺得飽就停。national（國家的）、modern（現代的）、common（常見的）都不能形容吃東西的感覺。

passages.zh: 星期六晚上，我和表哥 Leo 去士林夜市。Leo 說：「我餓到這裡的東西全都吃得下！」我們先吃了一大塊炸雞，接著吃臭豆腐、蚵仔煎，還喝了珍珠奶茶。Leo 一直吃個不停。「你確定你沒事嗎？」我問。「沒問題。」他拍拍肚子說。一個小時後，Leo 坐在椅子上，一臉難過。「我肚子好痛，」他說，「我吃太多了。」我買了一瓶溫水給他，他慢慢喝，但接著他說：「有東西從我喉嚨衝上來了！」我們及時衝進廁所。回家的路上，Leo 非常安靜，連小吃攤都不想看。「下次，」他說，「我覺得飽了就會停。」

passages.title: 書包有多重
passages.text: Every morning, Jenny carried a huge backpack to school. It had all her textbooks, a laptop, two water bottles, and a lot of snacks. One day, her {1} hurt so much that she could not raise her arms. Her mom took her to see a doctor. The doctor asked her to stand on a scale with her backpack, and then without it. "Your backpack is twelve kilos!" he said. "That is almost a third of your {2}. It is too {3} for a girl your age. It can hurt your back, your {4}, and even your knees." Then he gave her some advice. "Only bring the books you need each day, and carry your backpack on both shoulders, not just one." Jenny listened. She took out the snacks and left some books at school. Now her backpack is much lighter, and her shoulders don't hurt anymore. "My {5} feel better too," she said. "I can finally run to catch the bus!"

blanks.why: 書包太重，「肩膀」痛到手舉不起來 her shoulders hurt。tickets（票）、villages（村莊）、bills（帳單）都不會痛。
書包十二公斤，差不多是她「體重」的三分之一 a third of your weight。village、ticket、holiday（假期）都不能用公斤來比較。
too heavy「太重」。quiet（安靜的）、bright（明亮的）、polite（有禮貌的）都不能形容書包的重量。
太重的書包會傷到背、「脖子」和膝蓋 your back, your neck, and even your knees，都是身體部位。bill、meal（一餐）、museum（博物館）不是。
前面醫生說過書包會傷到膝蓋，現在「膝蓋」也好多了，可以跑去趕公車 My knees feel better。tickets、bills、letters（信）不會「覺得好一點」。

passages.zh: 每天早上，Jenny 都背著一個超大的書包上學，裡面有她所有的課本、一台筆電、兩個水壺，還有一大堆零食。有一天，她的肩膀痛到手都舉不起來。媽媽帶她去看醫生。醫生要她背著書包站上體重計，再放下書包量一次。「你的書包有十二公斤！」他說，「差不多是你體重的三分之一。對你這個年紀的女生來說太重了，會傷到你的背、脖子，甚至膝蓋。」接著他給了她一些建議：「每天只帶需要的書，而且書包要用兩邊肩膀背，不要只背一邊。」Jenny 聽了醫生的話，拿出零食，把一些書留在學校。現在她的書包輕多了，肩膀也不痛了。「我的膝蓋也好多了，」她說，「終於可以跑去趕公車了！」

passages.title: 睡錯姿勢的早晨
passages.text: Last Monday, I woke up and could not turn my head. My {1} was stiff, and it hurt every time I moved. "You slept the wrong way," Mom said. I had to go to school like a robot. When my friends called me, I had to turn my whole body to look at them. They thought it was {2}. During PE class, I could not play basketball, so I sat and watched. The teacher put a warm towel on my {3} and said, "Relax. It will be better in two days." That night, Grandma came to visit. She rubbed my {4} gently with some oil. It smelled strong, but it worked. The next morning, I could turn my head again. "Thank you, Grandma!" I said. She smiled and told me to use a {5} pillow. Since then, I have never had a stiff neck.

blanks.why: 頭轉不動，因為「脖子」僵硬 My neck was stiff。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、letter（信）不會僵硬、也不會痛。
轉整個身體看人，朋友覺得很「奇怪」strange。thirsty（口渴的）、hungry（餓的）、lonely（孤單的）都不能形容「這件事」。
把熱毛巾放在「肩膀」上 put a warm towel on my shoulders。bills（帳單）、meals（餐點）、museums（博物館）都不是身體部位。
阿嬤用油幫我揉「脖子」rubbed my neck。corner（角落）、ticket、village 不能揉，也和落枕無關。
落枕常是枕頭太高，所以要用「低一點的」枕頭 a lower pillow。noisier（比較吵的）、richer（比較有錢的）、braver（比較勇敢的）都不能形容枕頭。

passages.zh: 上週一，我一醒來頭就轉不動了。我的脖子很僵硬，每動一下就痛。「你睡姿不對，落枕了。」媽媽說。我只好像機器人一樣去上學。朋友叫我的時候，我得轉動整個身體才能看他們，他們覺得很奇怪。體育課我不能打籃球，只能坐著看。老師把一條熱毛巾放在我肩膀上，說：「放輕鬆，兩天就會好一點了。」那天晚上，阿嬤來我們家，她用一些藥油輕輕地揉我的脖子。味道很重，但很有效。隔天早上，我的頭又可以轉了。「謝謝阿嬤！」我說。她笑了笑，叫我改用低一點的枕頭。從那之後，我再也沒有落枕過。

passages.title: 害羞的烏龜
passages.text: My little sister has a pet turtle named Bubu. Bubu is very {1}. Whenever someone comes close, he pulls his head and long {2} into his shell. My sister wanted to see his face, so she tried many things. She called his name, sang songs, and even danced. Nothing worked. Then I gave her an idea. "Turtles like to feel safe. Just sit quietly and be {3}." So she sat on the floor and put a small piece of lettuce in front of him. Ten minutes passed. Her {4} started to hurt, but she did not move. Finally, Bubu's head came out slowly. He stretched his {5} and ate the lettuce. My sister had the biggest smile. "He trusts me now!" she said in a soft voice. Since then, Bubu comes out every time he sees her.

blanks.why: 有人靠近就縮進殼裡，表示牠很「害羞」shy。loud（大聲的）、rich（有錢的）、noisy（吵鬧的）都和「躲起來」的行為不符。
把頭和長長的「脖子」縮進殼裡 pulls his head and long neck into his shell。ticket（票）、meal（一餐）、bill（帳單）不是烏龜的身體部位。
前面說「安靜地坐著」，所以要「有耐心」be patient。careless（粗心的）、rude（沒禮貌的）、noisy（吵鬧的）都和「安靜等待」相反。
坐在地上等很久，「膝蓋」開始痛 Her knees started to hurt。tickets、museums（博物館）、letters（信）不會痛。
stretch one's neck「伸長脖子」去吃菜葉。village（村莊）、corner（角落）、bill 都不能「伸長」。

passages.zh: 我妹妹養了一隻叫做布布的烏龜。布布非常害羞，只要有人靠近，牠就把頭和長長的脖子縮進殼裡。妹妹想看看牠的臉，試了很多方法：叫牠的名字、唱歌，甚至跳舞，可是都沒用。後來我給她出了個主意：「烏龜喜歡有安全感，你只要安靜地坐著，有耐心一點。」於是她坐在地上，在牠面前放了一小片生菜。十分鐘過去了，她的膝蓋開始痛，但她一動也不動。終於，布布的頭慢慢地伸了出來。牠伸長脖子，吃起了生菜。妹妹笑得好開心。「牠現在信任我了！」她輕聲說。從那之後，布布每次看到她都會探出頭來。

passages.title: 爬玉山的下山路
passages.text: Last summer, my dad and I climbed Jade Mountain, the highest mountain in Taiwan. Going up was hard, but we were excited. We reached the top at sunrise. The view was so {1} that I forgot how tired I was. Going down was a different story. After two hours, my {2} started to hurt. Every step down felt like a small hammer hitting them. "Walk slowly and bend your knees a little," Dad said. He gave me his walking sticks. Then he took my backpack and carried it on his {3}. "Dad, now your bag and my bag are both on you!" I said. "Don't {4}. I'm strong," he smiled. When we got to the bottom, my legs were shaking, and my {5} was making loud noises. We went to a small restaurant and ate two big bowls of beef noodles. It was the best meal of my life.

blanks.why: 景色太「美妙」，讓我忘了累 so wonderful that I forgot how tired I was。stupid（愚蠢的）、cheap（便宜的）、lonely（孤單的）都不會讓人忘記疲累。
下山兩小時後「膝蓋」開始痛，後面也說要彎一點膝蓋。tickets（票）、letters（信）、villages（村莊）不會痛。
把背包背在「肩膀」上 carried it on his shoulders。bills（帳單）、museums（博物館）、meals（餐點）上面不能背東西。
Don't worry.「別擔心」，後面接「我很強壯」。order（點餐）、marry（結婚）、bake（烘烤）都接不上。
到山下肚子餓，「肚子」咕嚕咕嚕叫 my stomach was making loud noises，接著去吃牛肉麵。corner（角落）、ticket、village 不會因為餓而發出聲音。

passages.zh: 去年夏天，我和爸爸爬了台灣最高的山——玉山。上山很辛苦，但我們很興奮。日出時我們登上山頂，景色美得讓我忘了自己有多累。下山就是另一回事了。走了兩個小時後，我的膝蓋開始痛，每往下走一步，就像有一把小鐵鎚在敲它們。「慢慢走，膝蓋稍微彎一點。」爸爸說。他把他的登山杖給我，接著又拿走我的背包，背在他的肩膀上。「爸，現在你的背包和我的背包都在你身上了！」我說。「別擔心，我很強壯。」他笑著說。到了山下，我的腿一直發抖，肚子也咕嚕咕嚕大聲叫。我們走進一家小餐廳，吃了兩大碗牛肉麵。那是我這輩子吃過最棒的一餐。

passages.title: 健康課上的外星人
passages.text: Zork was an alien student from planet Glorp. On his first day at a Taiwanese junior high, he went to health class. The teacher was talking about the human body. "This is your {1}," she said, pointing to a picture. "It connects your head to your body." Zork raised his hand. "On my planet, we don't have necks. Our heads sit right on our {2}." Everyone laughed. "Then how do you look behind you?" asked a boy. "Easy. We have eyes on the back of our heads too," Zork said. The teacher went on. "Food goes down your {3} and into your stomach." Zork looked {4}. "Only one stomach? We have three {5}. One for breakfast, one for lunch, and one for dessert!" After class, all the students wanted to be his friend. They asked him a hundred questions about Glorp.

blanks.why: 「連接頭和身體」的部位是「脖子」neck。ticket（票）、museum（博物館）、village（村莊）都不是身體部位。
沒有脖子，所以頭直接長在「肩膀」上 Our heads sit right on our shoulders。bills（帳單）、letters（信）、meals（餐點）不合理。
食物經過「喉嚨」進到胃 goes down your throat。pocket（口袋）、corner（角落）、bill 都不是食物經過的地方。
聽到人只有一個胃，Zork 看起來很「驚訝」surprised。crowded（擁擠的）、delicious（好吃的）、cheap（便宜的）不能形容人的表情。
外星人有三個「胃」three stomachs，早餐、午餐、甜點各一個。tickets（票）、villages、corners 不能裝食物。

passages.zh: Zork 是一個來自 Glorp 星球的外星學生。他到台灣的國中上學的第一天，上了一堂健康課。老師正在講人體。「這是你們的脖子，」她指著一張圖說，「它連接頭和身體。」Zork 舉手說：「在我的星球上，我們沒有脖子，我們的頭直接長在肩膀上。」大家都笑了。「那你們要怎麼看後面？」一個男生問。「很簡單，我們後腦勺也有眼睛。」Zork 說。老師繼續上課：「食物經過你們的喉嚨，進到胃裡。」Zork 看起來很驚訝。「只有一個胃？我們有三個胃，一個裝早餐、一個裝午餐、一個裝甜點！」下課後，所有同學都想跟他做朋友，問了他一百個關於 Glorp 星球的問題。

passages.title: 海盜肩上的鸚鵡
passages.text: Captain Red was the scariest pirate on the sea, but he had a secret. He was afraid of the dark. Every night, his parrot, Polly, sat on his {1} and sang to him until he fell asleep. One stormy night, Polly had a cold. Her {2} was sore, and she could not sing at all. Captain Red could not sleep. He walked around the ship and felt {3}. His men noticed. "Captain, are you okay?" asked the cook. Captain Red was too proud to tell them his {4}. But the cook understood. He made Polly some warm honey tea. She drank it, and soon she felt better. She flew back to the captain and sang a soft song. Captain Red smiled and closed his eyes. The next morning, the men found their captain asleep with the parrot sleeping on his {5}.

blanks.why: 鸚鵡站在船長的「肩膀」上 sat on his shoulder，這是海盜和鸚鵡的經典畫面。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、meal（一餐）上面不能站鸚鵡。
感冒了「喉嚨」痛，所以完全不能唱歌 Her throat was sore。pocket（口袋）、corner（角落）、bill（帳單）不會痛。
怕黑又沒有歌聲陪伴，所以覺得「緊張不安」felt nervous。delicious（好吃的）、crowded（擁擠的）、expensive（昂貴的）不能形容人的心情。
開頭說他有一個「祕密」（怕黑），太驕傲不肯說出祕密 tell them his secret。garbage（垃圾）、traffic（交通）、meal 都不合理。
鸚鵡睡在他的「肚子」上 sleeping on his stomach。bill、ticket、museum（博物館）都不是身體部位。

passages.zh: 紅船長是海上最可怕的海盜，但他有一個祕密：他怕黑。每天晚上，他的鸚鵡波莉都會站在他的肩膀上唱歌，直到他睡著。一個暴風雨的夜晚，波莉感冒了，喉嚨很痛，完全不能唱歌。紅船長睡不著，他在船上走來走去，覺得很不安。他的手下發現了。「船長，您還好嗎？」廚師問。紅船長太驕傲了，不肯說出自己的祕密。但廚師明白了，他幫波莉泡了一杯溫熱的蜂蜜茶。波莉喝完後很快就好多了，她飛回船長身邊，唱了一首輕柔的歌。紅船長笑了，閉上眼睛。隔天早上，手下們發現船長睡得正熟，鸚鵡就睡在他的肚子上。

passages.title: 低頭族的脖子
passages.text: Ryan loved his phone. He played games on it before school, during lunch, and late at night. He always looked down at the small screen. One morning, his neck felt so stiff that he could not look up at the board in class. When he tried, a sharp pain went from his neck down to his {1}. His teacher sent him to the school nurse. The nurse said, "When you look down at your phone, your head is like a heavy ball. Your {2} has to hold it up for hours." Then she showed him a picture of a man with a round back. "If you don't {3} your habits, your back may look like this." Ryan was scared. From that day on, he held his phone higher, at the level of his eyes. Every thirty minutes, he stopped and turned his {4} slowly from left to right. He also put his phone {5} at ten every night. A month later, he felt much better. "I can see the board again," he said. "And I can see the sky too!"

blanks.why: 痛從脖子一路傳到「肩膀」went from his neck down to his shoulder。ticket（票）、bill（帳單）、museum（博物館）都不是身體部位。
低頭時，頭像一顆重球，要靠「脖子」撐住 Your neck has to hold it up。village（村莊）、meal（一餐）、letter（信）不能撐住頭。
change one's habits「改變習慣」。bake（烘烤）、marry（結婚）、borrow（借入）接 your habits 都不通。
每三十分鐘慢慢左右轉動「脖子」turned his neck。corner（角落）、ticket、garbage（垃圾）都不能「轉動」來放鬆。
put … away「把…收起來」：每晚十點把手機收起來。ahead（在前面）、abroad（在國外）、either（兩者之一）都不能和 put 搭配成這個意思。

passages.zh: Ryan 很愛他的手機，上學前、午餐時間、深夜都在玩手機遊戲，總是低頭看著小小的螢幕。有一天早上，他的脖子僵硬到上課時沒辦法抬頭看黑板。他一試，一陣刺痛就從脖子一路傳到肩膀。老師要他去保健室。護理師說：「你低頭看手機時，頭就像一顆很重的球，你的脖子得撐著它好幾個小時。」接著她給他看一張駝背男人的照片。「如果你不改變習慣，你的背可能會變成這樣。」Ryan 嚇壞了。從那天起，他把手機拿高到和眼睛同高；每三十分鐘就停下來，慢慢地左右轉動脖子；每天晚上十點也會把手機收起來。一個月後，他覺得好多了。「我又能看清楚黑板了，」他說，「而且也能看見天空了！」

passages.title: 會考前的胃痛
passages.text: The day before the big exam, Nina could not eat dinner. Her {1} felt strange, like there were butterflies flying inside it. "I'm so {2}," she said to her grandpa. "What if I forget everything?" Grandpa smiled and told her a story. "When I was young, I ran in a big race. Before it started, my {3} was dry, and my {4} were shaking. But when the race began, I forgot about all that. I just ran." "Did you win?" Nina asked. "No. I came in third," he laughed. "But I learned a {5} that day. Being nervous is normal. It means you care." Nina felt better. She ate a little rice and went to bed early. The next day, her stomach still felt a bit funny, but she did her best on every question.

blanks.why: 考前吃不下飯，「胃」怪怪的，像有蝴蝶在裡面飛 Her stomach felt strange。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、museum（博物館）不在身體裡。
擔心會忘光，所以很「緊張」nervous。cheap（便宜的）、crowded（擁擠的）、wet（溼的）不能形容考前的心情。
緊張時「喉嚨」很乾 my throat was dry。bill（帳單）、pocket（口袋）、corner（角落）放在這裡不合理。
緊張到「膝蓋」發抖 my knees were shaking。tickets、letters（信）、meals（餐點）不會發抖。
learn a lesson「學到一課、得到教訓」。garbage（垃圾）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不能用 learn a … 表示學到道理。

passages.zh: 大考前一天，Nina 吃不下晚餐。她的胃怪怪的，好像有蝴蝶在裡面飛。「我好緊張，」她對阿公說，「萬一我全部忘光怎麼辦？」阿公笑了，跟她說了一個故事：「我年輕的時候參加過一場很重要的賽跑。比賽開始前，我的喉嚨好乾，膝蓋一直發抖。可是比賽一開始，我就把這些全忘了，只顧著跑。」「你有贏嗎？」Nina 問。「沒有，我跑第三名，」他笑著說，「但那天我學到一課：緊張是正常的，那代表你在乎。」Nina 覺得好多了。她吃了一點飯，早早上床睡覺。隔天，她的胃還是有點怪怪的，但每一題她都盡了全力。

passages.title: 爸爸肩上的跨年煙火
passages.text: On New Year's Eve, my family went to see the fireworks at Taipei 101. There were thousands of people on the streets. It was so {1} that we could hardly walk. My little brother, Andy, was only five. He was too short to see anything. "I can only see people's backs!" he cried. So Dad lifted him up and put him on his {2}. Now Andy was taller than everyone. "I can see the building!" he shouted. At midnight, the fireworks started. Red, gold, and green lights filled the sky. Andy was so excited that he kept kicking his legs. "Ouch! My {3}!" Dad laughed. After twenty minutes, the show ended. On the way home, Andy fell asleep on Dad's back. Dad's shoulders and {4} were tired, but he was smiling. "Next year," he said, "you can sit on your mom's shoulders." Mom shook her head and said, "No way. I'll {5} the snacks."

blanks.why: 街上有好幾千人，所以非常「擁擠」so crowded that we could hardly walk。thirsty（口渴的）、honest（誠實的）、polite（有禮貌的）不能形容街道。
把弟弟扛到「肩膀」上 put him on his shoulders，弟弟就比大家都高。tickets（票）、villages（村莊）、bills（帳單）上面不能坐人。
弟弟坐在肩上亂踢，踢到爸爸的「脖子」My neck!。meal（一餐）、museum（博物館）、letter（信）不是身體部位。
扛了很久，爸爸的肩膀和「脖子」都累了。ticket、village、corner（角落）不會累。
媽媽不想扛人，說她負責「拿」零食 I'll carry the snacks。bake（烤）零食不是在現場做的事，marry（結婚）、paint（畫）接 the snacks 都不合理。

passages.zh: 跨年夜，我們全家去台北 101 看煙火。街上有好幾千人，擠到我們幾乎走不動。我弟弟 Andy 才五歲，太矮了什麼都看不到。「我只看得到別人的背！」他哭著說。於是爸爸把他抱起來，讓他坐在肩膀上。現在 Andy 比所有人都高了。「我看到大樓了！」他大喊。午夜一到，煙火開始了，紅色、金色和綠色的光照亮了天空。Andy 興奮得一直踢腳。「哎喲！我的脖子！」爸爸笑著說。二十分鐘後，煙火秀結束了。回家路上，Andy 趴在爸爸背上睡著了。爸爸的肩膀和脖子都很累，但他一直在笑。「明年，」他說，「你可以坐在媽媽的肩膀上。」媽媽搖搖頭說：「才不要，我負責拿零食。」

passages.title: 乳牛的四個胃
passages.text: On our class trip to a dairy farm, we met a cow named Daisy. She was eating grass slowly. "Did you know that a cow has four parts in its {1}?" asked the farmer. "First, the cow eats the grass quickly. Later, the grass comes back up its {2}, and the cow chews it again." "That's so {3}!" said Ken. The farmer laughed. "It helps her get more energy from the grass." Then he showed us how to milk a cow. I sat on a small chair and bent my {4}. My hands were too slow, and Daisy turned her big head to look at me. She had a bell around her {5}, and it rang every time she moved. Then she gave me a big lick on the face! Everyone laughed, and I laughed too. Now every time I drink milk, I think of Daisy and her four-part stomach.

blanks.why: 乳牛的「胃」分成四個部分 four parts in its stomach。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、letter（信）都不在牛的身體裡。
草會從「喉嚨」回到嘴裡再嚼一次 comes back up its throat。pocket（口袋）、bill（帳單）、corner（角落）都不是食物經過的地方。
吃下去又吐回來嚼，Ken 覺得很「奇怪」strange。polite（有禮貌的）、honest（誠實的）、thirsty（口渴的）不能用來評論這件事。
坐在小椅子上擠奶，要彎曲「膝蓋」bent my knees。tickets、bills、meals（餐點）不能彎。
鈴鐺掛在牛的「脖子」上 a bell around her neck。letter、village、museum（博物館）上面不能掛鈴鐺，也不會跟著牛移動。

passages.zh: 我們班校外教學去了一座酪農場，見到一頭名叫黛西的乳牛。牠正慢慢地吃著草。「你們知道乳牛的胃分成四個部分嗎？」農場主人問。「乳牛先很快地把草吃下去，之後草會從喉嚨回到嘴裡，牠再嚼一次。」「好奇怪喔！」Ken 說。農場主人笑了：「這樣能幫牠從草裡得到更多能量。」接著他教我們怎麼擠牛奶。我坐在一張小椅子上，彎著膝蓋。我的手太慢了，黛西轉過大大的頭看我。牠的脖子上掛著一個鈴鐺，每動一下就叮噹響。然後牠在我臉上大大地舔了一下！大家都笑了，我也笑了。現在我每次喝牛奶，都會想起黛西和牠那分成四個部分的胃。

passages.title: 卡在喉嚨的魚刺
passages.text: Grandma made steamed fish for dinner. It was my favorite dish. I was so {1} that I ate too fast. Suddenly, I felt something sharp in my {2}. A fish bone! I coughed and coughed, but it did not come out. Mom looked worried. Dad put his hand on my {3} and said, "Stay calm. We'll go to the hospital." At the hospital, the doctor asked me to open my mouth wide and say "Ahh." She used a small tool and took out the bone in ten seconds. It was long and thin. "You were {4}," she said. "If you swallow a bone like this, it may hurt your {5}. Next time, don't try to push it down with rice. Just come to see a doctor." On the way home, I said to Grandma, "Your fish is still my favorite. But next time, I will eat it slowly."

blanks.why: so hungry that I ate too fast「餓到吃太快」。polite（有禮貌的）、patient（有耐心的）、careful（小心的）都和「吃太快」相反。
魚刺卡在「喉嚨」something sharp in my throat。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、museum（博物館）都不在身體裡，放在這裡不合理。
把手放在我的「肩膀」上安慰我 put his hand on my shoulder。bill（帳單）、meal（一餐）、letter（信）都不是身體部位。
魚刺很快就被取出，醫生說你很「幸運」You were lucky。crowded（擁擠的）、cheap（便宜的）、noisy（吵鬧的）不能形容人的運氣。
吞下去的魚刺可能傷到「胃」hurt your stomach。museum（博物館）、corner（角落）、letter 不在身體裡。

passages.zh: 阿嬤晚餐做了清蒸魚，那是我最愛的菜。我餓到吃得太快，突然覺得喉嚨裡有個尖尖的東西——是魚刺！我咳了又咳，它就是不出來。媽媽看起來很擔心。爸爸把手放在我的肩膀上說：「保持冷靜，我們去醫院。」到了醫院，醫生要我把嘴巴張大說「啊」。她用一個小工具，十秒鐘就把魚刺夾了出來，那根刺又長又細。「你很幸運，」她說，「如果吞下這樣的刺，可能會傷到胃。下次不要用飯把它吞下去，直接來看醫生就好。」回家路上，我對阿嬤說：「你做的魚還是我的最愛，但下次我會慢慢吃。」

passages.title: 長頸鹿寶寶
passages.text: A baby giraffe was born at a zoo last spring. When she was born, she fell almost two meters to the ground! But she was fine. Within an hour, she stood up on her long, thin legs. Her {1} shook a lot at first, but soon she could walk. The zookeepers named her Lulu. Every day, visitors came to see her. Lulu was {2} about everything. She stretched her {3} over the fence to look at the children. Giraffes have very long necks, but did you know they have only seven bones in them, just like humans? Lulu's mother often lowered her head and helped her reach the leaves on tall trees. One day, Lulu ate so many leaves that her {4} became round. The zookeepers {5} when they saw her. Now she is almost three meters tall, and she still looks at every child who comes to visit.

blanks.why: 剛出生站起來，「膝蓋」一直發抖 Her knees shook。tickets（票）、museums（博物館）、letters（信）不會發抖。
be curious about…「對…感到好奇」，後面說她伸長脖子看小朋友。cheap（便宜的）、crowded（擁擠的）、delicious（好吃的）不能形容動物的個性。
stretch one's neck「伸長脖子」越過圍欄。village（村莊）、bill（帳單）、meal（一餐）不能伸長。
吃太多葉子，「肚子」變得圓滾滾 her stomach became round。corner（角落）、ticket、village 不會因為吃東西變圓。
管理員看到她圓滾滾的樣子都「笑了」laughed。baked（烤）、married（結婚）、borrowed（借）都不合理。

passages.zh: 去年春天，一隻長頸鹿寶寶在動物園出生了。她出生的時候，從將近兩公尺高的地方掉到地上！但她沒事，不到一小時，她就用細長的腿站了起來。一開始她的膝蓋抖得很厲害，但很快就會走路了。管理員幫她取名叫露露。每天都有遊客來看她。露露對什麼都很好奇，她會把脖子伸過圍欄看小朋友。長頸鹿的脖子很長，但你知道嗎？牠們的脖子裡只有七塊骨頭，和人類一樣！露露的媽媽常常低下頭，幫她吃到高高樹上的葉子。有一天，露露吃了太多葉子，肚子變得圓滾滾的。管理員看到她都笑了。現在她將近三公尺高了，還是會盯著每個來看她的小朋友。

passages.title: KTV 唱了五小時
passages.text: After the last exam, our class went to a KTV to celebrate. We booked a big room for five hours. At first, everyone was shy. Then Jason picked a rock song and sang it very loudly. Soon everyone {1} him. We sang love songs, anime songs, and even old Taiwanese songs. We sang so much that we forgot to eat. Around eight o'clock, my {2} started to make noises, so we ordered fried chicken and French fries. By the end of the night, my voice was gone. My {3} hurt, and I could only whisper. My friend Mia had a different problem. She danced on the sofa during every song, and she hurt her {4}. The next morning, my mom heard my voice and said, "You sound like a duck!" I drank hot lemon tea all day, and my {5} got better slowly. It was a fun night, but next time I will sing for only three hours.

blanks.why: join someone「加入某人（一起做）」：大家很快就跟著一起唱。baked（烤）、married（嫁娶）、borrowed（借）接 him 都不合理。
忘了吃東西，「肚子」開始咕嚕叫 my stomach started to make noises。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、letter（信）不會餓。
唱到沒聲音，「喉嚨」痛，只能小聲講話 My throat hurt。pocket（口袋）、corner（角落）、bill（帳單）和聲音無關。
在沙發上跳舞，弄傷了「膝蓋」hurt her knee。museum（博物館）、meal（一餐）、ticket 不是身體部位。
喝熱檸檬茶，「喉嚨」慢慢好轉 my throat got better。letter、village、bill 不會因為喝茶而變好。

passages.zh: 最後一科考完後，我們班去 KTV 慶祝，訂了一間大包廂唱五個小時。一開始大家都很害羞，後來 Jason 點了一首搖滾歌，唱得超大聲，很快大家都跟著一起唱。我們唱情歌、動畫歌，甚至還唱了台語老歌，唱到連吃東西都忘了。八點左右，我的肚子開始咕嚕咕嚕叫，我們就點了炸雞和薯條。到了晚上快結束時，我的聲音不見了，喉嚨很痛，只能小聲說話。我朋友 Mia 有另一個問題：她每首歌都站在沙發上跳舞，結果弄傷了膝蓋。隔天早上，媽媽聽到我的聲音說：「你聽起來像一隻鴨子！」我喝了一整天的熱檸檬茶，喉嚨才慢慢好轉。那是很好玩的一晚，但下次我只唱三個小時就好。

passages.title: 柔道課的過肩摔
passages.text: Our PE teacher, Mr. Chen, used to be a judo player. One day, he taught us judo in the gym. "First, you must learn how to fall," he said. "If you fall the wrong way, you may hurt your head or {1}." We practiced falling on the soft mats again and again. Then he showed us a move called the shoulder throw. He held Tom's arm, turned around, and threw Tom over his {2}. Tom flew through the air and landed on the mat. "Wow!" everyone shouted. Tom stood up and laughed. "That was {3}!" Then it was our turn. I tried it with my friend Sam, but he was much heavier than me. I bent my {4} and pulled hard, but he did not move at all. Instead, we both fell down, and Sam landed on my {5}. "Ugh!" Mr. Chen helped me up and smiled. "Good try. Judo is not only about power. It is also about timing."

blanks.why: 摔倒方式不對，可能傷到頭或「脖子」hurt your head or neck。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、meal（一餐）不是身體部位。
過肩摔就是把人從「肩膀」上摔過去 threw Tom over his shoulder。bill（帳單）、museum（博物館）、letter（信）都不合理。
被摔飛還笑著說「好刺激」exciting。thirsty（口渴的）、hungry（餓的）、honest（誠實的）不能形容剛才的經驗。
用力拉之前要彎「膝蓋」bent my knees。tickets、meals（餐點）、villages 不能彎。
兩人一起跌倒，Sam 壓在我的「肚子」上 landed on my stomach，所以我才「呃！」一聲。corner（角落）、ticket、bill 都不是身體部位。

passages.zh: 我們的體育老師陳老師以前是柔道選手。有一天，他在體育館教我們柔道。「首先，你們要學會怎麼跌倒，」他說，「如果跌倒的方式不對，可能會傷到頭或脖子。」我們在軟墊上一次又一次地練習跌倒。接著他示範了一個叫做「過肩摔」的動作：他抓住 Tom 的手臂，轉身，把 Tom 從肩膀上摔過去。Tom 在空中飛過，落在墊子上。「哇！」大家都大叫。Tom 站起來笑著說：「好刺激！」然後輪到我們了。我和朋友 Sam 一組，但他比我重很多。我彎下膝蓋用力拉，他卻一動也不動。結果我們兩個一起跌倒，Sam 還壓在我的肚子上。「呃！」陳老師把我扶起來，笑著說：「不錯的嘗試。柔道不只是靠力氣，也要靠時機。」

passages.title: 阿嬤家的五樓
passages.text: My grandma lives on the fifth floor of an old building. There is no elevator, so she has to walk up and down the stairs every day. Last month, she told us her {1} hurt when she climbed the stairs. Mom was {2}. She wanted Grandma to {3} to our apartment, which has an elevator. But Grandma said no. "I have lived here for forty years. All my friends are here." So we found another way to help. Every Sunday, my brother and I go to her home and carry her groceries up the stairs. I usually carry the bag of rice on my {4}. It is heavy, but I feel strong. A doctor also taught Grandma some easy exercises to make her legs stronger. Now she does them every morning in the park with her friends. Last week, she climbed all five floors without stopping. "My {5} feel ten years younger!" she said with a big smile.

blanks.why: 爬樓梯時「膝蓋」會痛 her knees hurt。tickets（票）、villages（村莊）、letters（信）不會痛。
阿嬤膝蓋痛，媽媽很「擔心」worried。cheap（便宜的）、wet（溼的）、crowded（擁擠的）不能形容人的心情。
move to + 地方「搬到…」：希望阿嬤搬來有電梯的家。bake（烤）、marry（結婚）、borrow（借）都不能接 to our apartment 表示搬家。
把一袋米扛在「肩膀」上 carry the bag of rice on my shoulder。bill（帳單）、meal（一餐）、museum（博物館）上面不能扛東西。
做運動後一口氣爬上五樓，「膝蓋」感覺年輕十歲 My knees feel ten years younger。tickets、corners（角落）、letters 不會「覺得年輕」。

passages.zh: 我阿嬤住在一棟老公寓的五樓，沒有電梯，所以她每天都得走樓梯上下樓。上個月，她跟我們說爬樓梯時膝蓋會痛。媽媽很擔心，希望阿嬤搬來我們有電梯的公寓住，但阿嬤不肯。「我在這裡住了四十年，我的朋友都在這裡。」於是我們想了別的辦法幫忙。每個星期天，我和哥哥會去她家，幫她把買的東西搬上樓。我通常把那袋米扛在肩膀上，很重，但我覺得自己很有力氣。醫生也教阿嬤一些簡單的運動，讓她的腿更有力。現在她每天早上都和朋友在公園做運動。上星期，她一口氣爬完五層樓都沒有停下來。「我的膝蓋覺得年輕了十歲！」她笑得好開心。

passages.title: 水餃大胃王
passages.text: Our town held a dumpling-eating contest last weekend. The winner would get a big prize: a new bike. My brother Ben, who eats more than anyone I know, decided to {1} it. He did not eat breakfast that morning, so his {2} would have more room. There were ten people in the contest. Each of them had thirty minutes to eat as many dumplings as possible. When the contest started, Ben ate quickly. After fifty dumplings, he slowed down. After eighty, he stopped and held his {3}. A big man next to him was still eating. "Drink some water!" I shouted. Ben tried, but the water would not go down his {4}. In the end, the big man won with one hundred and twenty dumplings. Ben came in second. He got a {5} too: a free dinner at a dumpling restaurant. Ben looked at the card, put his hand on his stomach, and said, "Maybe next month."

blanks.why: enter a contest「參加比賽」，it 指前面的比賽。bake（烤）、marry（結婚）、borrow（借）接 it（比賽）都不合理。
不吃早餐，讓「胃」有更多空間 his stomach would have more room。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、letter（信）不能裝食物。
吃了八十顆撐不下，停下來抱著「肚子」held his stomach。corner（角落）、museum（博物館）、bill（帳單）不能抱著。
太撐了，水吞不下「喉嚨」would not go down his throat。pocket（口袋）、ticket、village 不是喝水經過的地方。
第二名也拿到一個「獎品」a prize：免費水餃晚餐。garbage（垃圾）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不能「得到」來當獎勵。

passages.zh: 上週末，我們鎮上舉辦了一場吃水餃比賽，冠軍可以得到一個大獎：一台新腳踏車。我哥哥 Ben 是我認識的人裡面最會吃的，他決定報名參加。那天早上他沒吃早餐，好讓胃有更多空間。比賽有十個人，每個人有三十分鐘，盡量吃越多水餃越好。比賽一開始，Ben 吃得很快。吃了五十顆後，他慢了下來；吃到八十顆時，他停下來抱著肚子。他旁邊一個高大的男人還在吃。「喝點水！」我大喊。Ben 試著喝，但水就是吞不下喉嚨。最後，那個大個子吃了一百二十顆奪冠，Ben 得了第二名。他也拿到一個獎品：一家水餃店的免費晚餐。Ben 看看那張卡，摸摸自己的肚子，說：「也許下個月再去吧。」

passages.title: 萬聖節的吸血鬼裝
passages.text: For the school Halloween party, I wanted to be a vampire. I wore a black cape and put on plastic teeth. My sister painted my face white. "You look scary!" she said. At the party, I met my friend Ivy. She was dressed as a doctor. "Stay away from me!" she laughed. "Vampires bite people on the {1}." I tried to say something scary back, but the fake teeth were too big. My words came out strange, and everyone laughed. Then the teacher brought out a big cake. I was {2}, so I took a piece. But I could not eat with the plastic teeth in my mouth. I took them out and ate the cake happily. A piece of cream fell on my cape and slid down near my {3}. Ivy laughed so hard that she held her {4}. "You're not scary at all," she said. "You're {5}!"

blanks.why: 吸血鬼咬人的「脖子」bite people on the neck。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、meal（一餐）都不是身體部位。
肚子「餓」了，所以拿了一塊蛋糕 I was hungry, so I took a piece。honest（誠實的）、polite（有禮貌的）、lonely（孤單的）和拿蛋糕沒有因果關係。
奶油掉在斗篷上，滑到「肚子」附近 near my stomach。bill（帳單）、museum（博物館）、letter（信）不在身上。
laugh so hard that … held one's stomach「笑到抱著肚子」。corner（角落）、ticket、village 不能抱著。
一點都不可怕，反而很「可愛」You're cute。crowded（擁擠的）、national（國家的）、wooden（木製的）不能形容人。

passages.zh: 學校的萬聖節派對，我想扮成吸血鬼。我穿上黑色斗篷，戴上塑膠假牙，姊姊幫我把臉塗白。「你看起來好可怕！」她說。在派對上，我遇到朋友 Ivy，她扮成醫生。「離我遠一點！」她笑著說，「吸血鬼會咬人的脖子。」我想說些可怕的話回她，但假牙太大了，說出來的話怪怪的，大家都笑了。接著老師拿出一個大蛋糕。我餓了，就拿了一塊，可是戴著塑膠假牙沒辦法吃。我把假牙拿出來，開心地吃起蛋糕。一塊奶油掉在我的斗篷上，一路滑到肚子附近。Ivy 笑到抱著肚子。「你一點都不可怕，」她說，「你好可愛！」

passages.title: 稻田裡的青蛙合唱團
passages.text: Every summer night, the frogs in the rice field behind my grandpa's house start their concert. "Ribbit! Ribbit!" They are so {1} that I can hear them from my bedroom. One night, Grandpa took me out with a flashlight to look at them. We found a small green frog on a rock. When it sang, the skin under its {2} got bigger and bigger, like a balloon. "That's how it makes such a big sound," Grandpa explained. "It works like a speaker." Then the frog jumped onto my {3}! I was so {4} that I almost dropped the flashlight. Grandpa laughed. "It likes you." I stood still, and after a minute, the frog jumped back into the water. On the way home, I tried to sing like a frog. I pushed air into my throat and made a funny sound. "Ribbit!" Grandpa laughed so hard that he held his {5}.

blanks.why: 在房間裡都聽得到，表示很「大聲」so loud that I can hear them。polite（有禮貌的）、honest（誠實的）、patient（有耐心的）和聽得到聲音無關。
青蛙叫的時候，「喉嚨」下面的皮膚會像氣球一樣鼓起來 the skin under its throat。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、bill（帳單）不是青蛙的身體部位。
青蛙跳到我的「肩膀」上 jumped onto my shoulder。meal（一餐）、museum（博物館）、letter（信）都不在我身上。
嚇一跳，「驚訝」到手電筒差點掉了 so surprised that I almost dropped the flashlight。cheap（便宜的）、crowded（擁擠的）、wooden（木製的）不能形容人。
笑到抱著「肚子」held his stomach。corner（角落）、ticket、village 不能抱著。

passages.zh: 每年夏天晚上，阿公家後面稻田裡的青蛙都會開演唱會。「呱！呱！」牠們叫得好大聲，我在房間都聽得到。有一天晚上，阿公帶我拿著手電筒出去看牠們。我們在一塊石頭上找到一隻綠色的小青蛙。牠叫的時候，喉嚨下面的皮膚越鼓越大，像一顆氣球。「牠就是這樣發出那麼大的聲音，」阿公解釋，「那就像一個喇叭。」接著，青蛙跳到了我的肩膀上！我嚇了一大跳，手電筒差點掉下去。阿公笑著說：「牠喜歡你。」我站著不動，一分鐘後，青蛙又跳回水裡。回家的路上，我試著學青蛙叫，把空氣擠進喉嚨，發出好笑的聲音：「呱！」阿公笑到抱著肚子。

passages.title: 灰姑娘的清潔機器
passages.text: In this story, Cinderella did not wait for a prince. Every day, her stepmother made her clean the whole house. She washed the floors on her hands and {1} for hours. Her {2} and {3} always hurt. One day, she had an idea. "I'm tired of doing this the old way," she said. She found some old wood and wheels in the garden and started to {4} a machine. It took her three weeks. Finally, the machine could clean the floor by itself. Now Cinderella did not need to get down on her knees anymore. News about the machine spread fast. Even the king wanted one for his palace. Soon, Cinderella opened her own {5} and sold her machines all over the country. She became rich and famous. One day, a prince came to buy a machine. He asked her to go to a ball with him. Cinderella smiled. "Sorry, I have too much work to do."

blanks.why: on one's hands and knees「跪趴著（用手和膝蓋撐地）」擦地板。tickets（票）、villages（村莊）、bills（帳單）不能撐在地上。
長時間跪著擦地，「脖子」和肩膀總是很痛。meal（一餐）、letter（信）、museum（博物館）不是身體部位。
「肩膀」痛 her shoulders always hurt，和前面的脖子並列。tickets、villages、bills 不會痛。
用木頭和輪子開始「建造、做」一台機器 build a machine。bake（烤）、marry（結婚）、cry（哭）都不能接 a machine。
open one's own business「自己開公司、創業」，接著賣機器到全國。garbage（垃圾）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不能「開」來賣東西。

passages.zh: 在這個故事裡，灰姑娘沒有等待王子。每天，繼母都要她打掃整間房子。她得跪趴在地上擦好幾個小時的地板，脖子和肩膀總是很痛。有一天，她想到一個主意：「我受夠用老方法做事了。」她在花園裡找到一些舊木頭和輪子，開始做一台機器。花了三個星期，這台機器終於可以自己清潔地板了。現在灰姑娘再也不用跪在地上了。這台機器的消息很快傳開，連國王都想要一台放在宮殿裡。不久，灰姑娘開了自己的公司，把機器賣到全國各地，變得又有錢又有名。有一天，一位王子來買機器，還邀請她一起去舞會。灰姑娘笑著說：「抱歉，我的工作太多了。」

passages.title: 飛機上的頸枕
passages.text: This summer, my family flew to Canada to visit my aunt. The flight was thirteen hours long! Before we left, Mom bought everyone a neck pillow. "You'll thank me later," she said. I thought it looked {1}, so I did not use it. After dinner on the plane, the lights went down. I tried to sleep sitting up. My head kept falling to one side, and I woke up with a stiff {2}. My little brother was sleeping happily with his pillow on. My dad was sleeping too, with his head on Mom's {3}. I could not sit still because my {4} were pressed against the seat in front of me. Finally, I took out the pillow and put it on. It was soft and warm. In five minutes, I was asleep. When I woke up, we were {5} in Canada. Mom smiled at me. "See? I told you."

blanks.why: 覺得頸枕看起來很「蠢」，所以不用 looked stupid。crowded（擁擠的）、thirsty（口渴的）、delicious（好吃的）不能形容頸枕的樣子。
頭一直歪向一邊，醒來「脖子」僵硬 a stiff neck。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、letter（信）不會僵硬。
爸爸把頭靠在媽媽的「肩膀」上睡 his head on Mom's shoulder。bill（帳單）、meal（一餐）、museum（博物館）不能靠著睡。
座位太擠，「膝蓋」頂到前面的椅背 my knees were pressed against the seat。tickets、museums、villages 都不是身體部位。
醒來時「快要」到加拿大了 we were almost in Canada。either（兩者之一）、quite（相當）、instead（反而）放在 in Canada 前面都不通。

passages.zh: 今年夏天，我們全家搭飛機去加拿大看阿姨，航程足足十三個小時！出發前，媽媽幫每個人買了一個頸枕。「你們之後會感謝我的。」她說。我覺得頸枕看起來很蠢，所以沒有用。在飛機上吃完晚餐後，燈光暗了下來。我試著坐著睡，頭卻一直歪向一邊，醒來時脖子僵硬得要命。弟弟戴著頸枕睡得很香，爸爸也睡著了，頭靠在媽媽的肩膀上。我沒辦法坐好，因為膝蓋一直頂著前面的椅背。最後，我拿出頸枕戴上，它又軟又暖，五分鐘內我就睡著了。醒來時，我們快到加拿大了。媽媽對我笑了笑：「看吧？我早就跟你說了。」

passages.title: 街舞社的第一堂課
passages.text: I joined the street dance club this semester. On the first day, our teacher, a college student named Leo, showed us a cool move. He rolled his {1} to the beat and then dropped down to the floor. "Your turn!" he said. I tried, but I looked like a robot with no oil. "Relax," Leo said. "Don't keep your legs straight. Bend your {2} a little and feel the music." I practiced again and again. After an hour, I was so {3} that I lay down on the floor. "Drink some water," Leo said. "And don't forget to stretch your {4} before you go home, or you will feel it tomorrow." He was right. The next morning, everything hurt. But I did not give up. Every day after school, I practiced in front of the mirror. One month later, I danced on the stage at the school {5}, and everyone cheered for me.

blanks.why: 跟著節拍轉動「肩膀」rolled his shoulders，是街舞常見動作。tickets（票）、villages（村莊）、bills（帳單）不能轉動。
腿不要打直，「膝蓋」稍微彎一點 Bend your knees。meals（餐點）、letters（信）、museums（博物館）不能彎。
練了一小時，「累」到躺在地上 so tired that I lay down。polite（有禮貌的）、honest（誠實的）、cheap（便宜的）和躺下來沒有因果關係。
回家前要伸展「脖子」stretch your neck，不然明天會痠痛。corner（角落）、ticket、village 不能伸展。
在學校的「園遊會、慶典」舞台上跳舞 at the school festival。garbage（垃圾）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不是可以上台表演的活動。

passages.zh: 這學期我加入了街舞社。第一天，我們的老師——一位叫 Leo 的大學生——示範了一個很酷的動作：他跟著節拍轉動肩膀，接著一下子蹲到地上。「換你們了！」他說。我試了一下，看起來卻像一台沒上油的機器人。「放輕鬆，」Leo 說，「腿不要打直，膝蓋稍微彎一點，感受音樂。」我一次又一次地練習。一個小時後，我累到直接躺在地上。「喝點水，」Leo 說，「回家前別忘了伸展一下脖子，不然明天你就知道了。」他說得沒錯，隔天早上我全身都在痛。但我沒有放棄，每天放學後都對著鏡子練習。一個月後，我在學校慶典的舞台上跳舞，大家都為我歡呼。

passages.title: 看診時的「啊」
passages.text: Last week, my little brother Leo got a cold. He had a fever, and his {1} was red and sore. Mom took him to the clinic. Leo was {2} of doctors. When the doctor said, "Open your mouth and say 'Ahh,'" Leo shut his mouth tightly. The doctor did not get angry. Instead, he took out a toy lion. "This lion has a sore throat too. Can you help him?" Leo nodded. "Lion, open your mouth!" he said. Then he opened his own mouth to show the lion. "Ahh!" The doctor quickly looked inside. "Good job!" Then he listened to Leo's chest and pressed gently on his {3}. "Does this hurt?" "No," said Leo. The doctor gave him some medicine and told him to drink a lot of water. Before we left, the doctor put a lion sticker on Leo's {4}. On the way home, Leo kept {5} it to everyone on the bus.

blanks.why: 感冒發燒，「喉嚨」又紅又痛 his throat was red and sore。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、museum（博物館）不會紅腫疼痛。
be afraid of…「害怕…」：他怕醫生，所以把嘴巴閉緊。honest（誠實的）、polite（有禮貌的）、cheap（便宜的）都不能接 of doctors。
醫生輕壓「肚子」問會不會痛 pressed gently on his stomach。bill（帳單）、letter（信）、corner（角落）不是身體部位。
把獅子貼紙貼在 Leo 的「肩膀」上 on Leo's shoulder。meal（一餐）、ticket、village 都不在他身上。
keep + V-ing「一直做…」：一直把貼紙「秀給」大家看 kept showing it to everyone。baking（烤）、marrying（結婚）、borrowing（借入）都不能接 it to everyone。

passages.zh: 上週，我弟弟 Leo 感冒了。他發燒，喉嚨又紅又痛，媽媽帶他去診所。Leo 很怕醫生，當醫生說：「嘴巴張開，說『啊』」時，Leo 把嘴巴閉得緊緊的。醫生沒有生氣，反而拿出一隻玩具獅子。「這隻獅子也喉嚨痛，你可以幫幫牠嗎？」Leo 點點頭。「獅子，嘴巴張開！」他說，接著自己張開嘴巴示範給獅子看：「啊——！」醫生趕快看了一下。「做得好！」然後醫生聽了聽 Leo 的胸口，輕輕壓他的肚子。「這樣會痛嗎？」「不會。」Leo 說。醫生開了一些藥，要他多喝水。離開前，醫生在 Leo 的肩膀上貼了一張獅子貼紙。回家的路上，Leo 在公車上一直把貼紙秀給每個人看。

passages.title: 偷吃雞蛋的蛇
passages.text: A farmer had a chicken house with many eggs. Every morning, some eggs were missing. One night, he hid and watched. A long snake came in through a small hole in the wall. It opened its mouth very wide and slowly swallowed a whole egg. The farmer could see the egg moving down its {1} like a ball. Then the snake swallowed another egg, and another. Its {2} now had three big round bumps. The snake was very {3}. It wanted to leave, but now it was too fat to go out through the small hole! It got stuck in the middle. The farmer laughed and carefully picked it up behind its {4}. He carried the snake to a forest far away and let it go. Then he {5} the hole in the wall. The snake never came back, but the farmer still tells this story with a smile.

blanks.why: 蛋像一顆球一樣滑下「喉嚨」moving down its throat。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、bill（帳單）不是蛇的身體部位。
吞了三顆蛋，「肚子」鼓起三個圓包 Its stomach had three big round bumps。letter（信）、museum（博物館）、meal（一餐）都不合理。
吃了三顆蛋，蛇很「飽」very full。crowded（擁擠的）、honest（誠實的）、polite（有禮貌的）不能形容吃飽的狀態。
從「脖子」後面抓起蛇，牠才咬不到人 picked it up behind its neck。corner（角落）、ticket、village 都不是身體部位。
fix the hole「把洞修好」，蛇才不會再進來。baked（烤）、married（結婚）、borrowed（借）接 the hole 都不合理。

passages.zh: 一位農夫有一間雞舍，裡面有很多雞蛋。但每天早上，總有幾顆蛋不見了。有一天晚上，他躲起來偷看。一條長長的蛇從牆上的小洞鑽了進來，牠把嘴巴張得好大，慢慢吞下一整顆蛋。農夫看到那顆蛋像一顆球一樣滑下牠的喉嚨。接著蛇又吞了一顆、再一顆，牠的肚子上鼓起了三個圓圓的大包。這條蛇吃得飽飽的，想要離開，可是牠現在太胖了，鑽不出那個小洞！牠卡在洞的中間。農夫笑了，小心地從脖子後面把牠抓起來，帶到很遠的森林裡放走，然後把牆上的洞修好。那條蛇再也沒回來過，但農夫現在說起這個故事時，還是會笑。

passages.title: 奶奶織的圍巾
passages.text: Last winter, my grandma knitted a scarf for me. It was bright yellow with a big red heart on it. When I saw it, I thought it was {1}. I did not want to wear it to school because my friends might laugh, so I put it in my closet. One morning, it was only eight degrees outside. My {2} was so cold on the way to school, but I still did not wear the scarf. The next day, my {3} was sore, and I could hardly talk. I had no {4}, so I put on Grandma's scarf. To my surprise, nobody laughed. Instead, my friend Sara said, "Where did you buy that? I want one too!" That evening, I called Grandma and asked her to teach me how to knit. On Sunday, we sat together on the sofa for hours. "Keep your {5} relaxed," she said, "and move your hands slowly." Now I am making a scarf for Sara.

blanks.why: 一開始覺得圍巾很「醜」，怕被朋友笑 I thought it was ugly。thirsty（口渴的）、hungry（餓的）、crowded（擁擠的）不能形容圍巾。
只有八度，「脖子」好冷 My neck was so cold。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、letter（信）不會覺得冷。
受寒之後「喉嚨」痛，幾乎說不出話 my throat was sore。bill（帳單）、meal（一餐）、museum（博物館）和說話無關。
have no choice「沒有選擇」，只好圍上圍巾。garbage（垃圾）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）不能用在 have no … 表示「不得不」。
織東西時「肩膀」要放鬆 Keep your shoulders relaxed。tickets、villages、bills 不能放鬆。

passages.zh: 去年冬天，奶奶幫我織了一條圍巾，亮黃色的，上面還有一顆大大的紅心。我一看到就覺得好醜，不想戴去學校，怕朋友笑我，就把它收進了衣櫃。有一天早上，外面只有八度，上學路上我的脖子好冷，但我還是沒有圍那條圍巾。隔天，我喉嚨痛到幾乎說不出話。我沒有選擇，只好圍上奶奶織的圍巾。沒想到，沒有人笑我，我的朋友 Sara 反而說：「你在哪裡買的？我也想要一條！」那天晚上，我打電話給奶奶，請她教我織圍巾。星期天，我們一起在沙發上坐了好幾個小時。「肩膀放鬆，」她說，「手慢慢動。」現在，我正在幫 Sara 織一條圍巾。

passages.title: 游泳課學蝶式
passages.text: This year, our swimming coach decided to teach us the butterfly stroke. "It's the hardest stroke," he said, "but it's also the most beautiful." First, he showed us how to move our arms. Both arms came out of the water at the same time and went forward. "Use your {1}, not just your hands," he said. Then he taught us the dolphin kick. "Keep your legs together. Don't bend your {2} too much." I tried my best, but I swallowed a lot of water. Every time I came up to breathe, I lifted my head too high, and my {3} started to hurt. "Look down, not forward," the coach said. "Move like a wave." After many weeks of practice, I finally swam twenty-five meters without stopping. I was so {4} of myself! That night, my arms were so tired that I could not even hold my spoon. Mom laughed and said, "Do you want me to {5} you?"

blanks.why: 划手時要用「肩膀」的力量 Use your shoulders。tickets（票）、villages（村莊）、bills（帳單）不能用來游泳。
海豚踢時「膝蓋」不要彎太多 Don't bend your knees。meals（餐點）、letters（信）、museums（博物館）不能彎。
換氣時頭抬太高，「脖子」開始痛 my neck started to hurt。corner（角落）、ticket、village 不會痛。
be proud of oneself「為自己感到驕傲」。cheap（便宜的）、crowded（擁擠的）、wooden（木製的）都不能接 of myself 形容心情。
手累到拿不動湯匙，媽媽開玩笑要「餵」我 feed you。bake（烤）、marry（結婚）、borrow（借）接 you 在這裡都不合理。

passages.zh: 今年，我們的游泳教練決定教我們蝶式。「這是最難的泳式，」他說，「但也是最美的。」首先，他示範手臂怎麼動：兩隻手同時離開水面，往前伸。「要用肩膀的力量，不要只用手。」他說。接著，他教我們海豚踢。「兩腿併攏，膝蓋不要彎太多。」我盡了全力，卻喝了好多水。每次抬頭換氣，我的頭都抬得太高，脖子開始痛。「往下看，不要往前看，」教練說，「像波浪一樣動。」練習了好幾個星期後，我終於一口氣游完二十五公尺。我好為自己驕傲！那天晚上，我的手累到連湯匙都拿不住。媽媽笑著說：「要不要我餵你？」

passages.title: 感冒的聖誕老公公
passages.text: On the night before Christmas, Santa Claus woke up with a terrible cold. His nose was red, and his {1} hurt so much that he could not say "Ho, ho, ho!" Mrs. Claus touched his head. "You have a fever. You must stay in bed," she said. "But the children are waiting for their gifts!" Santa said in a weak voice. So Mrs. Claus decided to go {2}. She put on Santa's red coat and hat. The big bag of gifts was very heavy, but she put it on her {3} and climbed into the sleigh. The reindeer were surprised, but they flew her all over the world. At every house, she left gifts and ate a cookie. By morning, she had eaten so many cookies that her {4} hurt. When she got home, Santa was feeling better. He had a warm scarf around his {5} and a cup of hot tea in his hand. "Thank you, dear," he said. "Next year, let's go together."

blanks.why: 感冒「喉嚨」痛到不能說「呵呵呵」his throat hurt。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、museum（博物館）不會痛。
go instead「代替（他）去」。either（也不）、quite（相當）、almost（幾乎）放在句尾都不能表示「代替」。
把一大袋禮物扛在「肩膀」上 put it on her shoulder。bill（帳單）、letter（信）、meal（一餐）上面不能扛東西。
吃了太多餅乾，「肚子」痛 her stomach hurt。corner（角落）、ticket、village 不會因為吃太多而痛。
圍巾圍在「脖子」上 a warm scarf around his neck。museum、meal、bill 都不能圍圍巾。

passages.zh: 聖誕夜前一晚，聖誕老公公醒來時得了重感冒。他的鼻子紅紅的，喉嚨痛到連「呵呵呵」都說不出來。聖誕婆婆摸摸他的額頭說：「你發燒了，一定要待在床上。」「可是孩子們都在等禮物啊！」聖誕老公公虛弱地說。於是聖誕婆婆決定代替他去。她穿上聖誕老公公的紅外套、戴上紅帽子。那一大袋禮物很重，但她把它扛上肩膀，爬上了雪橇。麋鹿們很驚訝，但還是載著她飛遍全世界。每到一戶人家，她就留下禮物，吃一塊餅乾。到了早上，她吃了太多餅乾，肚子都痛了。她回到家時，聖誕老公公已經好多了，他的脖子上圍著一條暖暖的圍巾，手裡拿著一杯熱茶。「謝謝你，親愛的，」他說，「明年我們一起去吧。」
